beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: Nothing new, just a title.

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing means choosing between context, skill, output or interface, and I had assumed I'd hand over the whole thing.

beats.trigger: Bring one example from your own organisation where people got access to a tool and did not use it.
beats.got: I need an example of a failed rollout. We have one, the Copilot licences.

beats.trigger: Test the switch assumptions and name one person and one test to take out of the room
beats.got: Nothing new. It's a verb list, though the one person and one test is concrete enough.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack?
beats.got: The question is which of four things to hand over. My honest first answer is the memory folder, which is exactly the shared-context problem I have.

beats.trigger: Your agent, skill, output or interface is a candidate for hire: does it do the job better than what they currently use?
beats.got: It's a jobs-to-be-done frame applied to my teammate. I know it from consulting.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: A usable check: the job file has to name one teammate and an outcome I could observe, or I send it back. I'd do this on the pricing working group.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Four sharing options, and the choice has to follow the outcome and not the tooling. That is the IT conversation I'm about to have.

beats.trigger: [Design the sharing plan](design-the-sharing-plan.md) finds what would stop that candidate from being absorbed and turns it into a technical plan plus a people plan.
beats.got: Nothing new, it's a link to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Find the one obstacle, then write two plans.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: The test for a real bottleneck is that it explains the others, not that it's the first problem I see. That pushes me away from the tech answer I'd default to.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: If my people plan has no names in it, the plan isn't done. Mine would have had no names.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans, imagines the failure, and writes the first real-world contact to `module-7/monday.md`.
beats.got: Nothing new, it points to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until tested.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: A sharper question than asking whether they'll adopt it. I can take it into the pricing group meeting.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in one person, one question and one test for Monday. That's useful.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: A good summary line, but it repeats what I already read in the exercise.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: Nothing new, it's the lecture title.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Our licence-activation dashboard counts access and calls it adoption.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: A good analysis can still die because leadership didn't own it. That worries me for the pricing pilot and our CFO.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily, but someone has to answer for the agent, and that doesn't copy.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: Each of the four options asks something different of the receiver. This mostly repeats the exercise.

beats.trigger: Not *how do I get them to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*
beats.got: Nothing new, this is the same switch question as in the exercise, reworded.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before I build more. Obvious once said, and I wouldn't have done it.

beats.trigger: It is rarely the same person across all four.
beats.got: Different teammates need different forms of sharing, which I can see on my team.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: Nothing new, it's a recap.

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: I have to come back with what the named person said, not with the plan.

take_homes: Don't hand people the whole agent. Pick one of four things (context, skill, output, interface) based on the teammate's job and the outcome they need.
Access isn't absorption. The bottleneck is usually people and ownership, not tech, and the plan needs named owners.
Before building more, talk to one person about how they do the job today and test one assumption about what would make them switch.

monday.move: Interview one pricing working group member about how they currently prepare the usage-pricing numbers, then test whether the pilot-cohort brief arriving in their usual channel beats their current routine.
monday.who: One working group member, probably the finance analyst who currently builds the pilot numbers by hand.
monday.when: Monday morning for the conversation, with the brief run on fresh data by Wednesday.
monday.stop_condition: If they say they would not open it, or still rebuild the numbers themselves, I stop and rethink the candidate before building anything more.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone keeps their own copy and I can't hand over shared context yet.

misconception.why: I came in thinking getting good meant better prompts. The module made the hard part ownership and who picks it up, not the prompt. It never argued against prompts directly, so I'm shaken, not changed.

one_line: Useful if you're about to roll something out to a team, because it makes you name who actually answers for it. The back half repeats itself, but the Monday question is worth it.
